source_text:
Ἐπειδὴ ἡ ἐκκλησία ἡ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τῆς Συρίας εἰρηνεύει, ὡς ἐδηλώθη μοι, διὰ τὴν προσευχὴν ὑμῶν, κἀγὼ εὐθυμότερος ἐγενόμην ἐν ἀμεριμνίᾳ θεοῦ, ἐάνπερ διὰ τοῦ παθεῖν θεοῦ ἐπιτύχω, εἰς τὸ εὑρεθῆναί με ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ὑμῶν μαθητήν.
πρέπει, Πολύκαρπε θεομακαριστότατε, συμβούλιον ἀγαγεῖν θεοπρεπέστατον καὶ χειροτονῆσαί τινα, ὃν ἀγαπητὸν λίαν ἔχετε καὶ ἄοκνον, ὃς δυνήσεται θεοδρόμος καλεῖσθαι: τοῦτον καταξιῶσαι, ἵνα πορευθεὶς εἰς Συρίαν δοξάσῃ ὑμῶν τὴν ἄοκνον ἀγάπην εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ:
Χριστιανὸς ἑαυτοῦ ἐξουσίαν οὐκ ἔχει, ἀλλὰ θεῷ σχολάζει. τοῦτο τὸ ἔργον θεοῦ ἐστιν καὶ ὑμῶν, ὅταν αὐτὸ ἀπαρτίσητε. πιστεύω γὰρ τῇ χάριτι, ὅτι ἕτοιμοί ἐστε εἰς εὐποιΐαν θεῷ ἀνήκουσαν. εἰδὼς ὑμῶν τὸ σύντονον τῆς ἀληθείας, δἰ ὀλίγων ὑμᾶς γραμμάτων παρεκάλεσα.
thought_title: Send a runner to Syria to glorify God
orientation: Ignatius, writing to Polycarp of Smyrna, has just learned that the church in Antioch is at peace and now asks Polycarp to convene a council and appoint a messenger to Syria.
pass_a_gloss: Since the church in Antioch of Syria is at peace, as was made known to me, through your prayer, I also became more cheerful in freedom from care of God, if indeed through suffering I attain God, so that I may be found in the resurrection your disciple. It is fitting, Polycarp most blessed by God, to convene a council most befitting God and to ordain someone, whom you hold very beloved and untiring, who will be able to be called a runner for God; to deem this one worthy, so that going to Syria he may glorify your untiring love to the glory of God. A Christian does not have authority over himself, but is devoted to God. This work is God's and yours, whenever you complete it. For I trust in the grace, that you are ready for good-doing belonging to God. Knowing your intensity for the truth, through few letters I exhorted you.

choices.why: Keeps the superlative force and the agent of blessing explicit, matching the Greek compound without hyphenating.
Renders the superlative adjective with its dative reference to God, preserving the sense of what is proper to God.
Keeps the compound's two elements visible in English, as the brief's literal lane requires, without smoothing into a paraphrase.

choices.english: in freedom from care of God
choices.why: Preserves the genitive 'of God' as the source or sphere of the carefreeness, matching the Greek word order and not resolving the ambiguity.
Keeps the noun 'good-doing' and the participle 'belonging to God' as separate elements, preserving the Greek structure.
rejected: for beneficence that pertains to God

pass_b_english: Since the church in Antioch of Syria is at peace, as I have been told, because of your prayer, I too have become more cheerful, free from care in God, if only through suffering I may attain God, so that I may be found in the resurrection as your disciple.

It is fitting, Polycarp, most blessed by God, to convene a gathering most befitting God and to ordain someone whom you hold very dear and who is untiring, one who can be called a courier for God. Deem this man worthy to go to Syria and glorify your untiring love for the glory of God.

A Christian has no authority over himself, but is devoted to God. This is God's work and yours, when you complete it. For I trust in grace, that you are ready for good-doing belonging to God. Knowing your intensity for the truth, I have encouraged you with few words.

problems.why: ἀμεριμνίᾳ θεοῦ means 'freedom from care by God' or 'God-given freedom from anxiety', not 'freedom from care of God' which suggests anxiety about God.

problems.quote: if only through suffering I may attain God
problems.why: The phrase means 'through the passion of God' (Christ's suffering), not 'through suffering I may attain God'.
problems.fix: if only through the passion of God I may attain
problems.ruling: θεοῦ ἐπιτύχω is 'attain God,' but διὰ τοῦ παθεῖν modifies the subject's suffering, not Christ's passion; 'passion of God' misreads syntax.

problems.why: τῆς ἀληθείας is 'the truth' (objective), not 'your truth'. The genitive ὑμῶν goes with σύντονον ('your intensity'), not ἀληθείας.
problems.ruling: εἰδὼς ὑμῶν τὸ σύντονον τῆς ἀληθείας: ὑμῶν modifies σύντονον ('your intensity'), not ἀληθείας ('the truth'), changing meaning.

edits.old: in freedom from care of God
if only through suffering I may attain God
edits.new: if only through the passion of God I may attain

edits.old: Knowing the intensity of your truth
edits.new: Knowing your intensity for the truth

problems.quote: convene a council most befitting God
problems.why: 'Council' here likely means a gathering or assembly, not an ecclesiastical council; reader may import later conciliar practice.
problems.fix: Use 'gather an assembly' or add a note.

edits.old: to convene a council most befitting God
edits.new: to gather an assembly most befitting God

problems.why: The same Greek term (theodromos) is rendered two different ways, making it unclear they are the same concept.
problems.fix: Pick one English rendering and use it consistently.

edits.old: one who can be called a God-runner
edits.new: one who can be called a runner for God

fixed: The confirmed problem about 'runners-for-God' was addressed by standardizing the rendering of theodromos to 'runner for God' in both the English and the literal gloss.

problems.why: Abstract noun 'Christianity' appears twice; reader may not grasp this is rare early usage.
problems.fix: Note that 'Christianity' as abstract noun is unusual and significant.

problems.why: 'Runner' (dromos) means courier or messenger, not athlete; but athletic metaphor follows.

edits.old: one who can be called a runner for God
edits.new: one who can be called a courier for God

fixed: Glossary problem about 'Christianity' is not a mistranslation; the source has Χριστιανισμός, which the brief's glossary renders 'Christianity', and the English uses it correctly.
Mistranslation: 'a runner for God' renders θεοδρόμος, which means a courier or messenger for God, not an athlete; changed to 'a courier for God'.

last_rejected.why: ἀμεριμνίᾳ is 'freedom from anxiety/care,' not 'God-given'; θεοῦ is genitive of association ('with God').
last_rejected.fix: in freedom from care with God
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν ἀμεριμνίᾳ θεοῦ reasonably rendered 'in God-given freedom from care'; genitive source is ambiguous.

last_rejected.quote: in the resurrection as your disciple
last_rejected.why: ὑμῶν goes with μαθητήν ('your disciple'), not ἀναστάσει; 'in your resurrection' misreads syntax.
last_rejected.fix: in the resurrection to be found your disciple
last_rejected.ruling: English 'in the resurrection as your disciple' correctly links ὑμῶν to μαθητήν, not ἀναστάσει.

last_rejected.why: ἄοκνος means 'not shrinking back, unhesitating, eager,' not 'untiring' (which suggests endurance).
last_rejected.ruling: ἄοκνος 'without shrinking/untiring'—'untiring' is within normal range; not a major error.

last_rejected.why: θεοδρόμος means 'one who runs for God / on God's errands,' not 'God-runner' (sounds like deity runs).
last_rejected.fix: God's runner or one who runs for God
last_rejected.ruling: 'God-runner' is a literal calque of θεοδρόμος; awkward but not misleading enough to be major.

last_rejected.why: καταξιόω takes double accusative: 'deem him worthy' or 'appoint him'; but 'this man' is object, infinitive clause follows.
last_rejected.fix: Deem him worthy, that going to Syria he may glorify
last_rejected.ruling: 'Deem this man worthy' correctly renders τοῦτον καταξιῶσαι; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: Again ἄοκνος as 'untiring' misrepresents; also 'your untiring love'—whose love? The church's, sent via delegate.
last_rejected.ruling: Same ἄοκνος issue; 'untiring love' is acceptable within word's range.

last_rejected.why: ἀνήκουσαν = 'befitting, appropriate to,' not 'belonging to'; εἰς εὐποιΐαν = 'for a good deed/act of kindness.'
last_rejected.fix: ready for an act of kindness befitting God
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνήκουσαν 'belonging to/befitting' overlap; 'belonging to God' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: σύντονος = 'compact, concise, intense' in sense of concentrated/earnest, but 'intensity for truth' is awkward.
last_rejected.fix: earnestness for the truth or concentrated zeal
last_rejected.ruling: σύντονος 'intense/earnest'; 'intensity for truth' is acceptable, not a major mistranslation.

polish.changed: Clarified the ambiguous phrase about attaining God through suffering, made the subject of the ordination sentence explicit, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving every claim and reference.

notes.quote: if only through the passion of God I may attain, so that I may be found in the resurrection as your disciple
notes.why: 'Passion of God' is ambiguous (God's suffering? Christ's passion?); 'attain' lacks object.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'through the passion [of Christ], which is God's [gift], I may attain [to God].'

notes.why: Same role (someone sent to Antioch) rendered differently in three letters.
notes.fix: Use one term or note the equivalence.

polish.changed: Clarified that the 'council' is a gathering of church leaders, kept 'courier' consistent, and smoothed the transition into the general maxim about a Christian's devotion to God.

notes.quote: A Christian has no authority over himself, but is devoted to God.
notes.why: Sudden general maxim interrupts specific instruction about envoy; 'authority over himself' opaque.
notes.fix: Connect to previous: the envoy must be wholly dedicated, not self-directed.

notes.why: Heading says 'runner' but text says 'courier'; same role, two words.

notes.quote: convene a council most befitting God
notes.why: 'Council' here likely means a gathering of church leaders, not a deliberative body.
notes.fix: Use 'gather a meeting' or 'convoke a gathering.'
